learning_objective: 🎯 Analyze how the world is shrinking! Learn how global economic and cultural flows affect our food, jobs, media, and everyday Indian life.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: It's the increasing interconnectedness of the world. It’s not just economic (trade and money); it’s also political, cultural, and technological (internet, migration).
India shifted from a state-controlled economy to a liberalized one. We opened our markets to foreign companies, reduced tariffs, and privatized many government sectors.
When global brands adapt to local cultures to sell better. For example, McDonald's selling McAloo Tikki or MTV broadcasting in Hindi and regional languages.
Globalisation has changed our tastes. Culture is increasingly tied to what we consume (brands, gadgets). Even traditional festivals are becoming highly commercialized corporate events.

fun_activity.title: 👕 The Label Hunt
fun_activity.instructions: Look at the manufacturing tags on the clothes, electronics, and shoes in your room. Write down all the different countries your items were made in. That list is globalisation in action!

exam_tips: 📌 Always define 'Glocalisation' with a clear, relatable example (food or media works best).
📌 Remember that Globalisation creates 'winners and losers'. The IT sector boomed, but traditional weavers and small farmers often suffered.
📌 Don't confuse Liberalisation (the policy of opening up) with Globalisation (the overall process of global integration).
quick_recap: ⭐ Transnational corporations (TNCs) produce and sell goods in multiple countries simultaneously.
⭐ The telecom revolution (cheap mobile phones/internet) has been the biggest driver of cultural globalization in India.
⭐ Globalisation doesn't mean we all become exactly Western; we mix global and local cultures together.
